title: Official Plan update launch and three development applications
subtitle: Also covered: bird-friendly city study, private street names, public art policy, debt write-offs and small business funding.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee recommended that staff begin work on a new Official Plan for Kitchener {{vote:m11}}. Staff described a multi-year process: technical studies and a community working group in 2024, drafting from early 2025, and a draft plan for Council in early 2026.

The committee also recommended approval of four planning applications. These cover a zoning change for a large greenfield subdivision on Gehl Place {{vote:m7}}, a 58-unit rental development on Windom Road {{vote:m8}}, a four-tower, 760-unit complex of up to 24 storeys on Huron Road {{vote:m9}}, and 26 large single-detached lots on Hidden Valley Road {{vote:m10}}. These items were noted as going to a Special Council meeting later the same day.

On other matters, the committee directed staff to study Kitchener becoming a Bird Friendly City {{vote:m1}}. It also recommended a revised public art policy {{vote:m6}} and a one-year extension of provincial funding for the Waterloo Region Small Business Centre {{vote:m5}}. Two sets of uncollectable accounts were written off {{vote:m3}} {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff be directed to start work on a new Official Plan for Kitchener, as set out in report DSD-2024-077.
The committee recommended adopting an Official Plan amendment raising the maximum height to 24 storeys and approving the matching zoning change for a four-tower mixed-use development.
The committee recommended an Official Plan amendment and zoning change allowing a multiple residential development with a floor space ratio of 1.4 and a height of 15.1 metres.

The committee recommended an Official Plan amendment, a zoning change and draft plan of condominium approval for a private-road development of large single-detached lots, with a corrected condition 13.
The committee recommended approving site-specific zoning standards for a draft-approved subdivision, including the updated Map No. 1 and a clause saying no further notice is required.
Staff were directed to investigate the benefits, feasibility and resource needs of Kitchener becoming a Bird Friendly City.
The committee recommended accepting revisions to public art policy GOV-COR-816 and adding five artworks at two City-run cultural facilities to the public art collection.

The committee recommended authorizing a one-year extension of the provincial funding agreement for the Waterloo Region Small Business Centre, with delegated signing authority for related program grant agreements.

debate: On Windom Road, a councillor asked for play space for the families the larger units may attract. The applicant's planner said nearby school playgrounds and a community centre are close, and that a small play area could be considered at site plan stage. Other councillors asked about tree loss, sustainability, school drop-off traffic and affordability. The applicant's planner said most trees would be removed and replaced through site plan, a traffic study found the impacts acceptable, and no units are planned as affordable.

On Huron Road, several councillors pressed for three-bedroom units in the towers. The applicant's planner said the unit mix is not final and the applicant would consider them, but cost makes them harder in high-rise rentals. Staff said unit mix is not regulated by zoning and the area lacks apartment-style housing. One councillor said the mix was reasonable given nearby low-rise housing and the cost of building larger units in towers.

A delegate from the neighbouring church on Huron Road objected to the height of the tallest towers near the church. The delegate also worried about loitering and litter on church grounds with no barrier. Staff said zoning requires no fence between two non-residential uses, because the buildings are set back 40 metres and a landscaped berm and parking structure sit between. A councillor suggested revisiting a barrier at site plan.

On Hidden Valley Road, a neighbouring landowner asked for a condition requiring a sanitary servicing easement. Staff and the applicant's planner opposed it, saying it was premature because the neighbouring lands' development potential is undecided and another servicing route exists. They preferred to deal with it at site plan. Residents' concerns about tree removal and drainage were addressed through a revised tree plan and grading design.

On the Official Plan update, councillors asked about engagement targets, reaching youth, newcomers and renters, and the risk of rework if the Region's planning role changes. Staff said the project is designed to adapt to that change and that a community working group would be recruited. They also said the work would cover water and wastewater capacity and the financial effects of growth.
